quiz.q: What shape is a candle flame on the space station?
quiz.why: Without gravity, hot gas does not rise, so the flame spreads evenly into a ball.

quiz.q: Why are space flames often blue?
options: Less soot is made, so less yellow glow
quiz.why: Yellow comes from glowing soot. Slow-moving 0g flames make much less soot.

quiz.q: A proposed Moon habitat has about how much oxygen?
quiz.why: Artemis designs use about 34% O₂ at 8.2 psi, so materials burn more easily.
Cool flames burn around 500–800 K and give off almost no light.

quiz.q: Why can ceiling smoke alarms struggle in space?
options: Smoke does not rise to the ceiling
quiz.why: With no buoyancy, smoke drifts slowly in every direction instead of rising.

quiz.q: How long can a message to Earth take from Mars?
quiz.why: Mars can be up to ~20 light-minutes away, so crews must act on their own.

quiz.q: Which gravity level has the LEAST fire test data?
quiz.why: Almost no experiments exist at Moon or Mars gravity. That is the research gap.

overview.title: Can fire burn in space?
overview.tip: Tap the stops on the map to fly the rocket! Which place do you think is the most dangerous for fire?

lab.title: Fire Lab: light a fire in space!
lab.desc: Pick a place, pick something to burn, and press Light it! Watch how the flame changes on Earth, in space, on the Moon and on Mars.
lab.tip: Press "Start" to learn with me, step by step. Then try to finish all 7 lab challenges!

solar.title: Sun Blasts! (real NASA data)
solar.desc: Sometimes the Sun blasts out light and tiny fast particles. These are called solar flares. Pick a real one from NASA and watch it fly to the astronauts!
solar.tip: Play "Storm Shelter": when the alarm rings, decide fast! Should the astronauts hide or keep working?

earth.title: What happens when a Sun storm hits Earth?
earth.desc: Make your own Sun storm! Pick how big it is, then press Launch and watch Earth’s invisible shield, the northern lights and the satellites.
earth.tip: Try the "Carrington 1859" storm. Can you make the northern lights shine over your city?

ranker.title: Burn Race: which one burns faster?
ranker.desc: Some things burn fast and some hardly burn at all. Pick two, guess the winner, and watch the race!
ranker.tip: Tip: fire-safe fabric and Teflon are very hard to burn. Guess right 3 times to become a Fire Detective!

gravity.title: Gravity Guess: fire on the Moon and Mars
gravity.desc: Scientists tested fire in space and on Earth, but never on the Moon or Mars! Can you guess what happens there?
gravity.tip: Look at the yellow dots on the left (space) and right (Earth). Your guess goes in the middle!

radar.title: Ghost Flame Hunt
radar.desc: Some flames are invisible! They are called cool flames. Use your radar to find them before your scans run out.
radar.tip: Ghost flames hide between the "no fire" squares and the "hot flame" squares. Look at the edges!

firegpt.title: Quiz Time with FireGPT
firegpt.desc: Answer fun questions about fire in space. You can also ask FireGPT anything!
firegpt.tip: Get 3 right in a row for a streak bonus! 5 or more earns the Space Scholar badge.

gaps.title: Be a NASA scientist: plan the next tests
gaps.desc: The red striped squares are places nobody has tested yet. You can pay for 3 experiments. Which ones will teach NASA the most?
gaps.tip: The Moon and Mars rows are super important, because astronauts will live there!

sources.title: Your Space Card collection
sources.desc: Every badge you earn flips a real NASA science card. Can you collect them all?
sources.tip: Open the trophy (top right) to see which badges you still need!

welcomeSteps.title: Hi, I’m Sparky!
welcomeSteps.text: I’m a robot firefighter. Fire acts super weird in space, and I need your help to learn about it!

welcomeSteps.title: Play and explore
welcomeSteps.text: Every part of this page is a game. Light fires, race materials, hunt invisible flames and launch Sun storms!

welcomeSteps.title: Earn badges
welcomeSteps.text: Play to win stars, XP and badges. Collect all the Space Cards to become Mission Fire Chief!
